brief.topic: Yusuf 12:86: taking your grief to Allah
brief.audience: Muslims who want a short, trustworthy daily reminder they can act on

coreInsight: In Yusuf 12:86, Ya'qub says he complains of his suffering and grief only to Allah: the grief we can't explain to people can still be taken to Him.

hooks.text: Some grief is hard to explain…
hooks.notes: Names a real feeling; the ayah answers it directly.

hooks.text: Who do you tell when it hurts?

hooks.notes: Intriguing but needs a second read.

selectionRationale: Most relevant and clearest at a glance; the teaching pays it off.

scenes.onScreen: Some grief is hard to explain… / Ya'qub's words in the Qur'an.

scenes.purpose: Teaching: the source, verbatim, with its reference.

scenes.onScreen: REFLECTION / Take it to Allah first. / Ya'qub's grief for his son was long and deep. In this ayah he says he brings his complaint to Allah. You don't need the right words. Tell Him what you can't tell anyone else, in your own language.
body: Ya'qub's grief for his son was long and deep. In this ayah he says he brings his complaint to Allah.
You don't need the right words. Tell Him what you can't tell anyone else, in your own language.

scenes.onScreen: Tell Allah what hurts today. / Share it with someone who is grieving
scenes.cta: Share it with someone who is grieving

caption.opening: Some grief is hard to explain, even to the people closest to you.
body: In Yusuf 12:86, Ya'qub says he complains of his suffering and his grief to Allah.
Tonight, in your own words and your own language, tell Allah what you couldn't tell anyone else.
caption.cta: Share it with someone who may be grieving quietly.

primaryCta.text: Share it with someone who is grieving

claims.text: Bringing what we can't explain to people to Allah in du'a is our reflection on the ayah.
